explanation: The development of cancer is characterized by the accumulation of a series of genetic mutations over time. Two major types of regulatory genes are implicated: proto-oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes. Proto-oncogenes stimulate cell division; when mutated, they transform into oncogenes, which are active at all times. In contrast, tumor suppressor genes function to inhibit cell division. Mutations that activate proto-oncogenes into oncogenes or deactivate tumor suppressor genes stimulate the cell cycle to progress uncontrollably, which ultimately leads to tumor formation.
